messages.body_plain:
Well ideally you would not. That plot (mutant ?) shows why one should not even think about using spreadsheet graphics. There is way too much 'chart junk',. aka 'crap', there. Google “Tufte chart junk” for a discussion
Generally one need a plot of the data or a table but not both and labelling the numeric data points in the actual plot is overkill, that is why there is a y-axis.
If you feel that you really need a table of the data as well as the graph (or vis versa for that matter see below.

##=========================================================
char1  <-   melt(chartjunk, id.vars = c("xx"))
g1 <-  ggplot(char1,  aes(xx, value, colour = variable )) +
             geom_line() + geom_g1  point()
g2 <- tableGrob(chartjunk)

grid.arrange(g1, g2, ncol=2)

##=========================================================

If you really need numbers on the graph itself us
g1 <-  ggplot(char1,  aes(xx, value, colour = variable )) +
             geom_line() + geom_g1  point()  +
            geom_text( aes(label = value))

I'am running R mainly using Rstudio + R Markdown on a desktop box (Dell precision T1600) and several servers (Dell 24core/256G RAM), all on Ubuntu 14.04 and R 3.1 or 3.2. Plots are mainly dot plots and bar charts with facets.

Is that what others observe, too ?

Either your data or your qplot command are wrong. There is no Espece
in the data.frame provided so the fill will fail. The data appear
to represent counts with the columns being the species, so there should
be something in the qplot command to tell it not to bin the data within
Semaine, but the data are still in the wrong format even then.

I suspect you have sent a summary of your data, which will result in a
different answer to sending the actual data.

But here goes...

> #My first issue is exactly what you understood, i want all of these bars
> to total 100%

Given the data supplied I would convert the the three species columns
into percentages to begin with:

data1 <- data2

data2[,c("Obs","Mega","Marmo")] <-
data2[,c("Obs","Mega","Marmo")]*100/rowSums(data2[,c("Obs","Mega","Marmo")])

then change the data.frame to long format...

library(reshape2)
mdata<-melt(data2,id.vars="Semaine",variable.name <http://variable.name>="Espece")

and then (sorry I don't use qplot, so I'm sticking with ggplot here)..

ggplot(mdata,aes(x=Semaine,y=value,fill=Espece))+geom_bar(stat="identity")

Alternatively, without converting the data into percentages:

mdata<-melt(data1,id.vars="Semaine",variable.name <http://variable.name>="Espece")
ggplot(mdata,aes(x=Semaine,y=value,fill=Espece))+geom_bar(stat="identity",position="Fill")

But that gives a 0-1 rather than 0-100 scale (could probably be
modified by relabelling a scale?).

> #My second one is purely visual, i want my bars on the middle of the
> graph (centered from week 47 to 9) and not at both sides.

I assume therefore that the data are weeks of the year and
that the 1-9 are from the year after the 47-53? You could
make week a factor:

mdata1$week <- factor(mdata1$Semaine,levels=c(47:53,1:9))
ggplot(mdata1,aes(x=week,y=value,fill=Espece))+geom_bar(stat="identity",position="Fill")

If your actual data aren't in the form of the data2 counts sent, I
suspect they are more like:

ddd<-do.call(rbind,apply(data1,1,function(x){data.frame(Semaine=rep(x[1],sum(x[2:4])),Espece=rep(c("Obs","Mega","Marmo"),times=x[2:4]))}))

data2) as does this:

ggplot(ddd,aes(x=week))+geom_bar(aes(fill=Espece),position="Fill")+ylab("Proportion")+xlab("Week")

> Hope it works

No it didn't, and you really should have checked that before sending it.
I'm only having a play with this as I have some other stuff running,
otherwise I would have stopped as soon as the example failed.

I'm not as grumpy as that last paragraph sounded.

messages.body_plain:
Hi:

I don't know if I have much to offer here, but I did a little
experiment with your code, starting by reducing the size of the legend
title to see if it were easier to spot changes in positioning by
slightly modifying the code.

ggplot() +
          geom_bar(data=test.melt, aes(x = Treatment, y = Abundance,
fill = Species), stat="identity", colour="black") +
          scale_fill_manual(values= getPalette(colourCount), breaks=n1) +
          xlab("Treatments") +
          ylab("Relative Abundance") +
          ggtitle("Some Title") +
          theme_bw() +
          theme(axis.text=element_text(size=12),axis.title=element_text(size=14,face="bold"),

                legend.title = element_text(size=8, face="bold"),

                plot.title = element_text(size=20, vjust = 2, face="bold"))

Changing vjust and hjust inside the element_text() call for
legend.title had no effect on the legend title at all. I tried 0, 1
and 2 as values of hjust and 0, 1, 2, 10, -10 for vjust inside
element_text() with no effect on the title.

Next, I tried guide_legend() and had some partial success:

last_plot() + guides(fill = guide_legend(title.hjust = 2))     #
results in movement of the title (so did 1)
last_plot() + guides(fill = guide_legend(title.vjust = 2)      # no
change in vertical positioning

Any value in the previous set for vjust applied with this call had no
effect on the legend title. When you make the legend title size 16pt,
then its horizontal adjustment no longer 'works' when legend_guide()
is called.

In the case of horizontal adjustment, I imagine that the size of the
legend box constrains the movement of the title text when it is 16pt
in size. The same may apply to the vertical adjustment, but the lack
of movement with any of the calls above seems a bit suspicious to me.
I'm not willing to call it a bug, but you might want to file an issue
on the ggplot2 issues page regarding vertical adjustments in legend
titles...unless someone comes up with a more satisfying answer.

Dennis
